claim: Within that single DSAL lineage the two scrapes disagree on 5.5% of entry-language assignments across the 18 languages whose labels map one-to-one, against the 10.3% IC-E-001 measures between the DSAL lineage and the digitization MelaKeela ships.
locator: 04-AUDITS/dedr-lineage-check.py, output 04-AUDITS/dedr-lineage-check.csv; same 18-language mapping and same method as 04-AUDITS/domain-e-dedr-digitisation-check.py
notes: Per language the within-lineage rate runs 2.0% (Tamil) to 14.3% (Kolami) across the 18 AGGREGATE languages. That range EXCLUDES Brahui, which is mapped separately because it is the language the published figure is about; the Brahui cell is DEDR-L-007 and it cuts against this row. The direction of the disagreement is also uneven and is stated so it is not read as symmetric noise: of the 1,414 disagreeing entry-language pairs, 465 are in dedr.csv only and 949 in dedr_new.csv only, so two thirds of it is material the 2026 re-parse has and the deprecated 2013 dump lacks. That is consistent with the older table being less complete rather than the newer one being noisier, and only dedr_new.csv participates in IC-E-001's 10.3%. This row therefore does NOT license subtracting 5.5 from 10.3: the two percentages are computed over different pairs of tables, and whether the disagreeing pairs are the SAME pairs in both comparisons has not been tested. What the row supports is a magnitude comparison and nothing arithmetic. Corrected after adversarial review; the omission of the Brahui cell is logged as BF-015.

claim: For Brahui specifically - the one language the published figure is about - the two scrapes of the DSAL lineage disagree on only 2.2% of entries, against the 8.2% IC-E-002 measures between the lineages.
locator: 04-AUDITS/dedr-lineage-check.csv, row Brahui: 1 dedr.csv-only, 5 dedr_new.csv-only, 268 shared of 274; IC-E-002 for the 8.2%
notes: Written as its own row under BF-011's control: the measurement that cuts against the working hypothesis gets a register row, not a line of prose. It cuts twice. First, on Brahui the within-lineage noise is about a quarter of the cross-lineage gap, not the 'roughly half' that the 5.5-against-10.3 aggregate suggests, so the parse-noise explanation is WEAKEST precisely where the page's number lives. Second, it means the site's 262 is further from both DSAL figures (269, 273) than they are from each other, which is what a genuinely separate lineage would look like - and therefore mild evidence FOR the independence that DEDR-L-005 records as untested, in the direction that would make IC-E-001 a real disagreement. Neither conclusion is drawn: n is 274 entries and one language, and DEDR-L-006 stands.
